title: Open Research Without Scale Feeds Your Competitor
documentTitle: Musk–Karpathy Email Thread: Top AI Institutions Today (Exhibit 14)
excerptForBlog:
OpenAI is on a path of certain failure relative to Google. There obviously needs to be immediate and dramatic action or everyone except for Google will be consigned to irrelevance.

It seems to me that OpenAI today is burning cash and that the funding model cannot reach the scale to seriously compete with Google (an 800B company). If you can't seriously compete but continue to do research in open, you might in fact be making things worse and helping them out 'for free', because any advances are fairly easy for them to copy and immediately incorporate, at scale.

The most promising option I can think of would be for OpenAI to attach to Tesla as its cash cow. I believe attachments to other large suspects (e.g. Apple? Amazon?) would fail due to an incompatible company DNA. Tesla already built the 'first stage' of the rocket with the whole supply chain of Model 3 and its onboard computer. The 'second stage' would be a full self-driving solution based on large-scale neural network training, which OpenAI expertise could significantly help accelerate. I cannot see anything else that has the potential to reach sustainable Google-scale capital within a decade.

Either we fix things and my engagement increases a lot or we don't and I will drop to near zero and publicly reduce my association. I will not be in a situation where the perception of my influence and time doesn't match the reality. — Elon Musk, forwarding Andrej Karpathy's analysis, January–February 2018

lessonTitle: Open Research Without Scale Feeds Your Competitor
situation: In early 2018, Elon Musk forwarded an internal analysis from Andrej Karpathy about OpenAI's competitive position against Google. Musk's message argues OpenAI is on 'a path of certain failure,' proposes attaching OpenAI to Tesla as a 'cash cow,' and warns he will otherwise drop his involvement 'to near zero.' The stakes: OpenAI's structure, funding model, and Musk's continued association.
insight:
Musk is doing a cold capital math check. Google is an '800B company'; OpenAI is 'burning cash.' In that gap, openness stops being a virtue and becomes a leak — 'any advances are fairly easy for them to copy and immediately incorporate, at scale.' The hidden move is recognizing that **research advantage without distribution and compute is a gift to whoever already has both**.

The Tesla proposal follows the same logic. He rejects Apple and Amazon on 'incompatible company DNA' and picks Tesla because self-driving gives the research a product wrapper that funds itself. This is classic **build-vs-attach** thinking: if you can't independently reach the scale of capital your competitor commands, you must fuse with something that already generates it. The closing ultimatum makes clear he treats his personal brand as a scarce asset that must not exceed his real influence.
application: Audit what you give away for free. If a well-funded incumbent can absorb your output faster than you can monetize it, either close the work, tie it to a product that compounds, or attach to a partner with the cash engine you lack. Decide before your best ideas become someone else's roadmap.
pullQuote: If you can't match a giant's scale, publishing your best ideas is a subsidy to them, not a strategy against them.
leadershipTraits: thinks in capital, not just ideas
